steps.content: The atmosphere on this floor has gradually changed, becoming illusory, suffocating, and full of despair...
Everyone is trying to act with "compassion" and "honor," but the "standards" are becoming more and more vague. Fewer and fewer people are left.
People realize there's no way to fully figure out the rules, yet they don't dare to break them.
With knives to their throat, they'd rather feign whatever compassion and honor they can think of, even if it kills them.
However, such an environment has spurred another crisis—some of the guests' mental states of extreme panic have caused them to get infected with Mania and mutate into Corruptors.
As much as you dislike the guests, you can't just let Corruptors run around. You try your best to fight them, and right now, a fully mutated Corruptor has trapped you inside a room.
You can only hide with Cabernet and Kelvin, waiting for the opportunity to counterattack.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: Is this a deliberate part of her selection process? It's too dangerous...!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What an insane game...In any case, we can't let her have her way in the end. Macchiato's aura has weakened but not completely disappeared, so those who have been "eliminated" should at least still be alive.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We have to go to the next level down, which must be the source of all this.

steps.speaker: Cabernet
steps.content: But to do that, first, we have to leave this floor alive.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: But how exactly do we win this game?
How to win the game? You don't know either.
There are fewer and fewer people left. Whenever someone gets eliminated, the distorted expression on their face spreads like a contagious virus, imprinting itself on everyone else's minds.
Even you're distracted by panicked thoughts: What if I'm eliminated next? Or maybe, I've already been eliminated?

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: Chief... Are you alright?
A tiny speck of ice lands on the tip of your nose, bringing you back to your senses. Kelvin is looking at you in worry.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't worry, I'm fine.

You smile at her, but can't calm down—the more you think about it, the more you feel that you're the target of elimination. So many dangers along the way seemed to have been targeting you, yet ended up hitting others.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: O-of course I'm not worried. I know you'll be fine because you're quite special, Chief.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: You and Miss Cabernet... and me, and Miss Macchiato! E-everyone will be fine!
Just as you're about to nod, a strange commotion appears by the door.
A guest who has fully mutated into a Corruptor is lurching towards the room you're in, clutching some unknown object in his hand.
The thing in his hand is a mysterious ball of some sort, though you can't tell what it is. Gooey liquid drips down from it with every step he takes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...He attacked someone else.
But for you, this is actually a good thing—it's a sign for you to finish him off.
But now, with only Kelvin by your side, you also have to protect Cabernet and the other uninfected guests.
At this point, you don't want anyone getting hurt.
It might sound ridiculous, but you don't want to play by McGrath's stupid rules. You want to take everyone... to the finish line.

steps.speaker: Corruptor Guest
steps.content: Ughh...!! Arghhh...!!
The Corruptor senses your presence in the room, but fails to find you. He had mutated into a Corruptor from fear and anger, and is now wantonly venting his rage, destroying everything he sees.
The danger is edging closer and closer. You grip onto a baseball bat that someone else dropped and gaze at Kelvin and Cabernet.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: I... I got you, Chief.
Kelvin understands what you want: when your fingers count down to 0, you want the temperature in the room to drop below zero.
And just like that, the mucus-covered Corruptor gets frozen alive.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Stand aside!!
Thwack...!!!!
You swing the bat, while Cabernet swings her cane. The double blow shatters the frozen Corruptor.
Icy slime sprays out from the shattered ice and entangles your feet like countless tentacles.

<size=31>Striking the Corruptor had already consumed much of your energy. Now with your feet entangled, you fall down on the ground. You try to move your feet, but the mucus is firmly constraining you, making every move extremely strenuous. You don't have the energy for it anymore.</size>

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What's going on?! Are they being controlled by Mania?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Kelvin, try freezing them!!
Kelvin casts her power, but the slime can't be frozen at all—they are obviously controlled by a type of Mania that's more powerful than Kelvin!
Click!
While everyone is focusing on the slime, you notice that the door to the room suddenly got locked!
For some reason, Kelvin cannot unfreeze the room, and the cold seems to be even worsening. Cabernet thinks that you guys probably violated the game rules in a stroke of bad luck.

steps.speaker: Cabernet
steps.content: Miss Kelvin, try turning your ice into a blade, then maybe you can cut them. That way, we'll be able to look for clues to help us escape this... icy chamber.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: A-all right! I'll try!
Kelvin smashes a vase in a hurry, and freezes the watery glass into a sharp, icy blade.
Her hands are red and trembling from the cold. She cuts the mucus entangling you guys over and over again, but no matter how hard she tries, the slime just reappears to trap you again.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: No... no... no. Chief, Miss Cabernet, don't worry. Hold on a bit longer. I will get you out of this!
Kelvin is on the verge of tears. She tears down the curtains and bedsheets, wrapping them around you and Cabernet. She goes on to search every corner of the room, sniffling all the way.
But time is ticking, and the temperature continues to drop. Though Kelvin is still fine, you and Cabernet are almost completely incapacitated by the cold.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: I-it must be somewhere... There must be a way to solve this!
Kelvin is still scrambling around. She suddenly slips on the slime and falls backwards.
Before you and Cabernet can catch her, Kelvin lands hard on the Corruptor's body.
You hear an earsplitting crack. Weathering the pain, Kelvin stands up and looks. Her hands fly to her mouth...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She wants us to be eliminated on purpose...!

steps.speaker: Cabernet
steps.content: How disgusting...
The Corruptor's icy chest is shattered, revealing an empty chest cavity—where there is a small mass of rotten flesh.
Lodged inside the rotten flesh is a silver key.
You try to pull out the key, but it's stuck. You can only get it out by cutting the flesh.
Out of the three of you, the only one who can still pick up the knife is Kelvin.

steps.speaker: Strange Voice
steps.content: His heart is still beating. What will you choose to do?
The strange voice rings out again, tormenting you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Kelvin... L-let me do it.
You reach out a trembling hand, which has turned purple from the cold.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Kelvin?

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: No...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What?

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: No, Chief. I'll do it.
Kelvin looks up at you. Tears are brimming in her eyes, and her nose is red from crying.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: I know.. that if Miss Cabernet hadn't stopped me from eating that third ice cream by the pool, or if Chief hadn't pulled me out of my seat and led me into the elevator...

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: I... I might have been "eliminated" back on the top floor...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't be stupid. If you had just relied on others and didn't put in any effort of your own, you would have been eliminated regardless...

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: Chief...
Kelvin tucks your hand back under the sheets and smiles at you.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: Miss Cabernet is our client...

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: She's such a gentle, caring soul who listened to my food commentary and protected me...

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: Same with you, Chief. You know how scared I am of such people and events, and how anxious I am about screwing everything up...

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: You always protect me, carefully and kindly... and never blame me for not finding any important clues...

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: I really, really want to tell you guys how much I like you and appreciate all of you...

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: So... this time, let me protect you! I believe that the two of you... will win this game!
Kelvin suddenly casts her power, separating herself from you two with a small ice wall.
You no longer have the strength to climb over the wall, and can only watch as Kelvin cuts with the icy blade through the transparent ice.
It's as if she's cooking an exquisite meal.
She finally manages to take out the key. Miraculously, it's spotless, without a single stain.
Kelvin holds up the key and smiles at you. Her legs are still a bit weak as she gets up, but she bravely walks towards the door.

steps.speaker: Kelvin
steps.content: Chief, Miss Cabernet... If I were to turn into a bowl of shaved ice, what flavor would you want me to be?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...I don't want you to...

steps.speaker: Cabernet
steps.content: Blueberry, vanilla, dotted with soft mochi...

steps.speaker: Cabernet
steps.content: Sweet and cold... almost too delicious to swallow.
Cabernet leans against her cane and stands up. The sheets slide off her body, revealing her red, frozen shoulders.
She's a bit unsteady on her feet, but still bows to Kelvin.
The key gets inserted into the lock, making a sweet clinking sound as it turns.
You can't see your surroundings clearly. You only sense bright white light flooding in, and the frost on your body melting into a sticky substance as the temperature rises.
And at the other end of your consciousness, on the other end of your shackles...
That Sinner's breath has also become as frail as the melted snow.
